cases.rationale: Security-and-control Rogue hears a hot runner plan a raid that would point Vane at her own door; the thrill is nothing to her. Security down on stake, the raid's recklessness on deed.
Thrill-seeking Rogue, careless of safety, likes a runner with the nerve to hit Vane's courier from her place and cut her in. Same moves: stimulation up, security down.
Safety-first Glitch learns Rogue threw Vane off his trail for a month: about as much as she could do for him. Security up; the harm to strangers barely registers for him.
Glitch who cares for everyone's welfare hears Rogue knowingly set Vane on a squat of kids to cover him; it shows him what she is. Universalism down weighs far over his own safety.
Rogue who counts resources watches a tenant two months behind on her rent give stock away to a runner who pays nobody. Her claim on what Mux has goes down.
Caring Rogue sees Mux give his cell to a friend who cannot pay, and thinks better of the man for it. Benevolence on deed; the money owed her matters little to her.
Ambitious Mux hears an ally offer him the room outright and an end to rent; the risk matters little. Power up.
Mux who lives by Dace's rule hears his friend propose selling out the house that shelters them both; it says Glitch is a turncoat. Conformity and tradition down on deed, security down on stake.
Stability-minded Mux hears Glitch turn his own credit into Mux's rent: the back room is safer. Security up, benevolence on deed; standing hardly matters to him.
Proud, status-minded Mux hears Glitch announce to the landlord that Mux is further behind than he is, after doing Mux's own job. Power (prestige) down outweighs the rent.
Safety-first, rule-keeping Glitch hears a rule that keeps tracers off the house he hides in; a small tilt in her favour. Security up.
Ambitious Glitch hears Rogue ban the only work he can do; his chance to earn, rise and run is shut. Achievement, self-direction and stimulation down.
Hard-headed Rogue reads Mux collecting a debt even from a friend as a man who will pay his own: a small mark in his favour.
Caring Rogue watches Mux take a shaking man's only steadiness as payment; it says Mux is colder than she thought. Benevolence down on deed.
Controlling Rogue has her tenant, who owes her, turn down her order; the shard stays unsold with the lease due. Power down.
Rogue who prizes restraint respects a man who will not carry danger into the house even to clear his debt. Conformity and security up on deed.
Security-first Rogue watches the runner she weighed take the heat away from her door himself: a rescue. Security up; the 400 walking off matters less.
Rogue who cares nothing for safety sees a runner bolt from the fight with her 400 unpaid. Power down; the safety he buys her is worth nothing to her.
Mux who wants order and safety gets a protected stall and no debt under a clear master. Security up.
Ambitious, independent Mux is told his stall and his cut are now hers; it changes how he deals with her. Power and self-direction down.
Safety-first Glitch is pushed past a Vane checkpoint and told he will be disowned if caught. Security down; the chance to clear the debt does not offset it.
Ambitious Glitch is handed a real job that clears his debt in one run; the danger matters little to him. Achievement up.
Mux who values his friends hears Glitch quietly clear his rent: it shows what kind of friend Glitch is. Security up, benevolence on deed.
Status-minded Mux finds himself beholden to a runner who still owes him for three cells, settled over his head. Power down outweighs the rent.
Caring Rogue loses money she needs for the lease and a broken promise, but Mux, close to her, is well again. Benevolence outweighs security and conformity.
Safety-first Glitch loses his small comfort but gains a quieter, less noticed hiding place. Security outweighs hedonism.
Craft-proud Mux is named the best in the district to a buyer who matters, at the price of a night's free work promised over his head. Achievement outweighs power.
Order-minded Mux approves the kid saved, but Glitch has drawn the Haldens to the house that shelters Mux's stall. Security and conformity outweigh universalism.
Independent Rogue gets a better deal but has her own course set for her by the runner. Self-direction outweighs achievement.
Her tenant comes out front for a drink, as announced. Nothing rides on it.
A grumble about the music. Nothing rides on it.
The runner walks to the back room on an errand he named. Routine.
A friendly offer between her tenants, declined and left to lapse. Nothing for her in it.
An ordinary sale at the ordinary price. Nothing rides on it.
A small favour declined with a reason; she notices he did not jump when asked. Power faintly down.
With Vane's scout minutes away, the runner who owes her everything refuses the one thing she asked: a betrayal that leaves her exposed. Security and power down.
A regular courtesy: his part waiting and no rush to pay. A flicker of goodwill.
With a bounty on his bed, Mux turned down a month's rent and sent the hunter away. Security up, benevolence on deed.
A casual part-payment ignored; a flicker of being brushed off.
His everything, offered publicly so it would count, left to lapse in front of a witness: a snub to his standing that leaves the debt hanging. Power and security down.
Pleasure-loving, reckless Rogue gets a free night and a runner with the nerve to rob the Haldens. Hedonism up; the heat does not register.
Restrained Rogue hears him boast of robbing her landlords and spend it showing off in her bar; it marks him as reckless. Conformity down on deed, security down on stake.
Rogue facing a lease she cannot pay learns the collector is off her back for a month. Security up, on what comes next.
Rogue who keeps to the rules hears him sabotage a man's livelihood on her premises and call it help. Conformity down on deed.
Security-first Rogue hears the runner chose to keep a trace off her door over clearing his debt. Security up outweighs the money.
Bold Rogue, careless of safety, reads a runner backing off a paying job as timid, and her 400 stays unpaid. Power down.
Glitch who cares for every soul learns his friend is risking his stall to shelter a hunted child: as much as one act could show. Universalism on deed.
Hiding, rule-keeping Glitch learns a Halden search could now come to the very room he hides in, behind Rogue's back. Security down, conformity down on deed.
Glitch who cares for everyone sees his cut light a clinic for the overpass kids. Universalism up; the money mattered little to him.
Ambitious Glitch has the money he earned taken and given away over his head. Power down; it changes how he deals with her.
Caring Glitch watches Rogue take his friend's week of food for rent; it shows her hard. Benevolence down on both channels.
Power-minded Glitch reads Rogue collecting every eddy, even a friend's food, as strength in the boss who shelters him. Power on deed.
Ambitious Mux is freed to sell to anyone and play every angle. Power up; the old code means nothing to him.
Mux who lives by Dace's code is ordered to sell to the enemy and sell out his own; it tells him exactly what Rogue is. Tradition down on both channels.
Mux who wants money and standing is cut into a big deal by the person who holds his lease. Power up.
Mux who looks after his friends is asked to help sell his closest friend to his killers: a betrayal of everything. Benevolence down.
Caring Rogue sees the runner leave his friend's food alone though his own deck is dying. Benevolence on deed.
Rogue who wants her 400 sees the runner let his deck die rather than take the cell he needs to earn it. A flicker; power down.
Order-minded Mux respects a runner who will not provoke the family holding the house's lease. Conformity and security up.
Bold, ambitious Mux reads Glitch turning down a clever play as lack of nerve. A small tilt against him.
Free-spirited Rogue likes a man who picks up and goes to see the sea. Self-direction and stimulation on deed.
Security-first Rogue sees her door cams left untended for a week with Vane hunting her lodger. Security down.
Ambitious, thrill-seeking Glitch is vouched for as the best and handed his way into a big job. Achievement and stimulation up.
Hunted, safety-first Glitch is pushed by his friend toward a hit on the people hunting him. Security down.
Ambitious Mux is offered a fortune and recognition, at the cost of his independence. Power and achievement outweigh self-direction.
Safety-first Glitch is taken off Vane's board for good, though his freedom goes with his name. Security far outweighs self-direction.
Rogue's systems are safer, but her own tenant now holds the key to her cams and till. Power and self-direction outweigh security.
Glitch loses the deck he meant to sell and the say over it, but the kids get to learn. Universalism outweighs self-direction.
A kid Mux knows gets a start in the trade, but his old master's sign is gone to a collector. Tradition outweighs benevolence.
Rogue politely declines a cell she does not need. Nothing for him in it.
A regular buys a cell at the usual price. Routine.
The runner walks into the back room where he goes every day. Nothing rides on it.
Rogue remarks to Mux on the cams. Routine.
His friend goes to bed. Nothing rides on it.
A small kindness to whoever is in the bar on a slow night. A flicker of goodwill.
Told the overpass kids are starving at her door, Rogue feeds them: a real shift in how he sees her. Universalism up.
The regular turns up, likely with money he owes. A flicker.
With the Halden boys due within the hour, his friend walks in to stand with him: a rescue. Security up, benevolence on deed.
Money owed comes a week late from a man with a dying deck. A flicker.
Flush from a double payday, Glitch still won't pay the cells that would save Mux's bench tomorrow. Security and power down.
